news.speaker: NWS New York forecast discussion
news.text:
.AVIATION /21Z TUESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
***Major Storm System to Impact Terminals Late this Afternoon into
Tonight***

Deepening low pressure over the Midwest will track up into the
eastern Great Lakes tonight, sending a strong frontal system across
the area. This will be a high impact event with strong winds and
heavy rains.

Ceilings will gradually lower to IFR through early this evening as
rainfall and winds increase across the terminals. Brief LIFR is
possible. Confidence on fog development remains low.

SE winds will ramp up through the night, reaching 25-30 G45-50kt,
highest at the coastal terminals. Highest winds will be after 00Z
and up until the cold frontal passage, which will be from west to
east from approximately 09Z to 12Z. Post-frontal WSW winds will
gusts 30-35kt, possibly a few higher gusts, especially Wednesday
afternoon. There could be a lull in the winds briefly as the front
moves through.

An isolated thunderstorms is possible overnight.

...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Changing of flight categories may vary by 1-3 hours.

A few gusts above 50kt will be possible from 03Z to 08Z. Highest
gusts potential is at KJFK.

Isolated thunderstorm possible overnight.

OUTLOOK FOR 18Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY...

Wednesday Afternoon: VFR. SW wind 20-25kt G30-35kt. Gusts gradually
decrease at night.

Thursday: VFR. WSW winds 10-15kt with gusts near 20kt.

Friday: VFR early, becoming MVFR or lower with rain. Increasing SE
winds late.

Friday Night: MVFR or lower. SE winds 15-25kt G30-40kt.

Saturday: MVFR or lower with rain. SE winds 20-30kt G30-40 kt,
becoming W 20-25kt G30-35kt.

Sunday...VFR. W 20-25kt G30-35kt.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts,
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

news.text:
.AVIATION /07Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
As deepening low pressure over the Great Lakes lifts into Eastern
Canada tonight, a strong frontal system will move through the
terminals. A secondary low forming nearby will lift to the north on
Wednesday.

Pre-frontal squall line with very heavy rain has passed through all
but KGON, with cond improving mainly to MVFR (vsby) in its wake.
KISP still IFR vsby but should also improve to MVFR shortly. A lull
in winds likely after the squall line passage with direction
shifting S and then backing SE before cold fropa from about 08Z-10Z.
Post-frontal WSW winds daytime Wed expected at 15-22G30-35kt, with
possibly a few higher gusts, especially in the afternoon.

Rain with MVFR vsby continues at the NYC metro terminals and KBDR
after the passage of a squall line, with IFR at KHPN/KSWF. KISP
still IFR at 06Z but should improve to MVFR shortly. IFR/LIFR vsby
and an isolated tstm still possible at KGON where the front has yet
to move through.

VFR cond will prevail daytime Wed, with the possibility of a few
brief showers with TEMPO MVFR cigs mid to late morning.

...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

AMD likely through the AM push for changing conditions.

.AVIATION /10Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
A cold front will move across this morning as low pressure moves
across Ontario and a secondary low moves across New England.

A band of showers marking the front was moving across northern NJ as
of 09Z, and should be through the NYC metro and Hudson Valley
terminals between 10Z-11Z, and across the Long Island and CT
terminals between 12Z-14Z. MVFR/IFR cond ahead of the front should
quickly improve to VFR with fropa, with gusty S flow shifting to the
WSW.

Delayed onset of stronger post-frontal WSW winds by a couple of
hours, with greatest likelihood of seeing G30-35kt after about 16Z-
17Z.

...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

conditions.
